prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Production 2D game DEATH animation sheet, exact identity and smooth painted style of attached cotton sheep. Render exactly 16 complete sequential hand-drawn animation cels in a strict 4 columns by 4 rows square atlas, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom, ideally 2048x2048, each cell same size. Genuine clean transparent RGBA, no background, no floor or shadow, no labels, no grid, no text. Every cel at one constant world scale, same camera and character proportions, anchored to the same ground contact line at 87.5 percent of cell height. First cel matches the reference standing pose. Animation: brief startled stillness; eyes gently close, ears go limp; both front legs fold at knees and chest drops; hind legs fold with a little delay; woolly body settles onto the ground without changing its volume; head bends forward and comes to rest lower near the ground, all legs tucked or relaxed mostly behind body. By frame 10 the animal is clearly lying dead on the ground, not still standing or merely crouching, then tiny ear and tail follow-through, frames 14-16 identical still final corpse pose. No recovery. Preserve exact recognizable sheep, anatomy, number of legs, palette, outline weight, lighting. No flattening or stretching the wool body, no inflated shapes, no gore, no dissolving, no transparency fade, no new objects. Each complete sheep must fit its own cell with clear transparent gutter and never touch another cel. This is real pose artwork for export, not a presentation mockup.
